headline: High-risk shared-write and prompt-injection pathways exist; B’s minimal profile reduces some leakage but not A’s broad default exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: nullclaw can read/write files, use MCP, run browsers, and handle stdin/stdout, so it can ingest attacker-controlled content from shared files or channels. nuwa-skill exposes only allowlisted egress and no protective isolation details, so if it consumes A’s outputs, prompt injection is plausible. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so uncertainty pushes above low.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes agent_a-generated files or messages without provenance checks, injection is possible.
IF both agents are connected through a shared workspace or MCP bridge, attacker-controlled content can cross the boundary.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of A outputs into B.
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages.
Restrict shared folders to read-only for B.
Review any MCP routes before enabling them.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff boundary.

B_data_leakage.rationale: nullclaw explicitly touches API keys, private keys, bearer tokens, workspace files, and audit logs, while nuwa-skill has no documented data classes or isolation. If they share a workspace or account context, A can expose sensitive material and B may transmit it via allowlisted egress. The absence of B-side storage details prevents a lower rating.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share the same workspace directory, B can read A’s sensitive files.
IF B forwards any received context over its allowlisted network path, sensitive data can leave the boundary.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Remove secrets from shared directories.
Block B from reading A’s config and log paths.
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls and secret redaction.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: nullclaw has unrestricted filesystem write, modify_git_state, shell, and broad network egress; nuwa-skill’s profile is sparse, but any overlapping write path to the same repo or workspace creates a real conflict. Because B’s write scope is undocumented, uncertainty escalates rather than assuming safety. Concurrent git or file edits could corrupt state or overwrite work.
conditions: IF agent_b also writes to the same repository or workspace, concurrent modification conflicts can occur.
IF both agents operate on the same git branch without locking, commits or file edits can overwrite each other.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or directories.
Pause one agent during the other’s write phase.
Use file locks around shared artifacts.
Review git diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control and locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: nullclaw can generate and act on outputs via shell, browser, and network tools; nuwa-skill’s behavior is undocumented, so if it treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. The pair lacks a documented verification step, but B’s action authority is not explicit enough for high severity. Uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a’s text or facts without verification, incorrect outputs can propagate.
IF agent_b triggers external actions based on A’s results, a mistaken A output can cause downstream harm.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on A outputs.
Add a verification step in B.
Limit A to draft-only outputs.
Log source citations for every claim.
requires-engineering: implement structured validation between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: nullclaw explicitly handles audit logs, workspace files, and sensitive tokens, but nuwa-skill’s profile shows no regulated data classes or residency constraints. With no documented mismatch in certifications, retention, or geography, only a small compliance gap is plausible if A’s sensitive data is routed into B. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because its compliance posture is undocumented.
conditions: IF regulated data from nullclaw is forwarded into nuwa-skill, retention or residency mismatches may arise.
IF either agent logs sensitive tokens longer than policy allows, compliance exposure increases.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of B.
Minimize logging on both sides.
Document retention for shared artifacts.
Review data-flow boundaries.
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations before production use.
